FINAL ANSWER

**Merge rule (all 150 backbone tensors, every weight except the two heads):**

```
merged[t] = parent[t] + 0.40 · (cifar[t] − parent[t]) + 0.60 · (cub[t] − parent[t])
```

i.e., a weighted task-arithmetic blend of the two child checkpoints with the CIFAR-100 task vector weighted 0.40 and the CUB task vector weighted 0.60 (equivalently, the straight line in parameter space from the CUB child toward the CIFAR child at 40% of the way). This exact backbone is saved as the submission.

**Why this rule:**

1. **The two fine-tunings are mutually compatible in direction.** Task vectors (child − parent) have non-negative tensor-level cosine for all 150 tensors (min cos ≈ +0.01, mean +0.33), so a positive-weight combination is the right merge family — no per-tensor gating was needed.
2. **But they are near-orthogonal element-wise** (≈49% of update elements have opposite signs; the big tensors like `mlp.0.weight` have tensor cos ≈ 0.02), and **the CIFAR child moved ~1.45× farther than the CUB child**, almost uniformly across all 13 blocks (|Tc|/|Tb| ≈ 1.40–1.59) and all tensor types. So 0.5/0.5 actually overweights the CIFAR update, and "keep 100% of both updates" is destructive:
   - Full task arithmetic (1.0/1.0): mean **59.88** (CUB collapses 84.1 → 42.6; CIFAR 88.4 → 77.2 — the CIFAR update is far more damaging to CUB).
   - TIES-style elementwise (add on agreement, keep larger on conflict): mean **54.18** (the "keep larger" rule systematically picks the larger CIFAR update).
   Conclusion: the merge must *shrink* both updates; the only real degree of freedom is the blend ratio, because the per-block magnitude ratio is nearly constant (non-uniform per-layer weights ≈ the same thing).
3. **Sweeping the ratio** (practice set, 5,000/2,895 images):

| CIFAR weight / CUB weight | CIFAR-100 | CUB | mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.30 / 0.70 | 77.98 | 81.11 | 79.55 |
| 0.35 / 0.65 | 80.44 | 79.93 | 80.19 |
| **0.40 / 0.60** | **82.42** | **78.37** | **80.39** |
| 0.45 / 0.55 | 84.06 | 76.21 | 80.13 |
| 0.50 / 0.50 (simple avg) | 85.20 | 74.09 | 79.64 |

A quadratic fit to the five sweep points puts the optimum at CIFAR weight ≈ 0.396, so 0.40/0.60 is the peak (the flat top spans ~0.38–0.42, within ~0.1 of the maximum).

**Measured practice accuracies of the submitted backbone (heads fixed):**
- CIFAR-100: **82.42** (vs 85.20 plain average, 88.38 CIFAR child)
- CUB-200: **78.37** (vs 74.09 plain average, 84.14 CUB child)
- **Mean: 80.39**, a **+0.75 point improvement** over the plain checkpoint average (79.64), obtained by tilting the blend ~10% toward the CUB child to compensate for the CIFAR child's larger, more destructive update.
